name: Small multiples on a shared axis
reader_question: How do several items' paths over time compare when each gets its own panel?
relationship: The same measure over the same periods for 4–6 items, one panel each, on an identical value axis so slopes and levels compare directly.
use_when: Overlaid lines would tangle but the reader must still compare shapes and levels
All panels share one unit, period set and basis
avoid_when: Only two or three series exist — use indexed-lines
Panels differ in unit or basis, which would force different axes

data_contract.notes: Measure and unit shared by every panel
One value axis applied to every panel; all values must fall inside it

units: One unit throughout; identical axis minimum, maximum and tick step in every panel, stated in the subtitle.

editable: One native line chart per panel, each with an embedded workbook (Edit Data)
Panel titles and last-value labels as text
not_data_bound: The shared axis is enforced by the renderer; after editing one panel's axis the others must be matched by hand
Panel titles and last-value labels are text boxes, not chart elements

table_alternative: A matrix of item by period with the unit in the header.
variations: A reference line at a stated threshold in every panel
limitations: A shared axis can flatten the smallest series
Six panels is the legible limit at slide size

excluded_alternatives.reason: Different axes make equal-looking slopes mean different things

excluded_alternatives.form: Single chart with six overlaid lines
